transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess... what finally pushed me to come in is just that my eating has been kind of all over the place lately. Some weeks I just... I barely touch dinner. And then other nights, I don't know, I just end up standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. So... yeah. That's mostly it.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight lately?

Um... I don't really know. I haven't been checking the scale. I guess it probably fluctuates a bit... just because of what I just said, with my eating being so back and forth. But... I'm not really sure.
Do you worry about gaining weight when you're eating?
Um... no, not really. I don't... I don't really think about that part of it.
Do you ever feel guilty after eating?
Um... no, not really. I just... eat, and then I go back to bed. I don't really feel much about it either way.
Do you usually eat those crackers and sweets when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Um... I don't know about stressed. It's just... my eating has been all over the place lately. I guess that's what finally pushed me to actually come in here. Some weeks I barely even touch dinner... and then other nights I'm just standing in the kitchen eating those crackers and sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. I don't really know why.
Do you eat those crackers and sweets when you're feeling upset?

I... I think I just said that. I don't really know if I'm upset. It's just... like I said, my eating is just all over the place. That's why I'm here. Sometimes I barely eat dinner for a week, and then... then I'm just eating crackers in the dark. I don't know why.
Are you using food to help yourself feel better when you're eating those crackers and sweets at night?

I... I really don't think it's about feeling better. Like I've been trying to say, it's just that my eating is completely unpredictable right now. That's the main reason I made this appointment. I just... I go from hardly eating dinner for days on end to... to just standing there in the kitchen at night with the crackers and sweets. I'm not trying to fix a mood, it just happens.
Are you eating at night because you can't sleep?

Not exactly. I mean... I am awake, but it's not like I'm lying there trying to sleep and failing. I just... I only really need about three or four hours right now. 

When I wake up, I actually feel pretty charged. So I just get up before the sun is even out and... I don't know, write blog posts or plan out projects. I'm just awake.
Do you feel hungry when you're not eating during the day?

Not really. I don't... I don't really notice if I'm hungry. Like I mentioned, that's kind of what finally pushed me to come in. The fact that my eating is just all over the place. Barely touching dinner some weeks, and then the crackers at night... I just don't really feel the hunger during the day, I guess.
Do you enjoy eating when you do eat?

I suppose not. Um... I used to enjoy cooking, but... it just feels like a chore now. I guess a lot of things do. Things I used to actually look forward to... my book club, going to galleries... even tending my rose beds. I just... I keep putting them off. It all just feels like work.
Is your lack of interest in things like cooking, book club, or tending your rose beds related to your eating patterns?

I don't know if it's related to the eating. I just... like I said, things I used to look forward to, they just feel like chores now. Cooking, the book club, the galleries... even the roses. I just keep putting them off. It's just... I don't know.
Do you think your eating patterns are connected to why things feel like chores now?

I... I'm really not sure if they're connected. I just know that... well, like I said, things I used to enjoy just don't appeal to me anymore. The book club, cooking... going to galleries, even my roses. It's just... it all just feels like a chore that I keep putting off. I don't know why.
Do you think your lack of interest in activities is related to your eating patterns?

I don't... I don't really know if the eating has anything to do with it. It's just... like I've been saying, it's just that the things I used to actually look forward to... the book club, cooking... the galleries, the rose beds... they just feel like chores now. I just... I keep putting them off. That's all.
Do you think you eat at night because of feelings or emotions?

I'm not sure if it's about feelings. It's just... that's actually what finally made me come in. My eating is just all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner at all. And then... other nights, I just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else is asleep. I don't really know why.
Do you think your mood has anything to do with when you eat or how much you eat?

I don't know about the eating... but I guess my mood gets... low. There are these stretches where the whole house just feels sort of gray and heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table feeling completely empty... even if nothing bad actually happened that day. I don't know if that's what makes me eat, though.
How often do you feel this low mood?

I don't know... it's hard to keep track of time when it gets like that. But I guess... if I had to add it all up, those gray periods... where I just feel guilty and can't find the energy for anything... it's probably been about seven months total.
Do you feel this low mood most of the day?
I guess... yeah. When it's like that, it's pretty much all day. Just... sitting there, feeling empty. Like I said, everything just feels heavy.
How many days in a row do you usually feel this low mood when it happens?

I don't know... it's just stretches of time. Like I said before... it just feels like the whole house is gray and heavy for a while, and I'll sit at the table feeling empty. It just keeps going like that... day after day, usually.
Is your low mood present every day, or are there days in between where you feel okay?

Not really... not when it's happening. Like I was saying, it's just these stretches. Every day is just... sitting at the kitchen table. Even if nothing terrible has actually happened that day... it still just feels empty.
